text: Sorting. Python's sorted() and list.sort() use Timsort, which takes O(n log n) time. Merge sort splits the list in half, sorts each half and merges them: always O(n log n). Quick sort is O(n log n) on average but O(n^2) in the worst case, for example when the pivot is always the smallest item.

Binary search works only on a SORTED array. Each step compares the target with the middle element and throws away half of the array, so the search space goes n -> n/2 -> n/4 -> ... -> 1. That takes about log2(n) steps, so binary search is O(log n). For 1,000,000 items that is only about 20 comparisons.
Binary trees. Each node has at most two children. The height of a balanced binary tree with n nodes is about log2(n). Inorder traversal of a binary search tree visits the values in sorted order.

Recursion. A recursive function must have a base case that stops the recursion. Without one, Python raises RecursionError after about 1000 nested calls. Naive recursive fibonacci recomputes the same values again and again, so it takes O(2^n) time. Memoization (store answers in a dict or use functools.lru_cache) makes it O(n).

Depth-first search (DFS) on a grid or graph. Keep a visited set and mark a cell as visited before exploring its neighbours; otherwise DFS keeps revisiting the same cells and never finishes. DFS takes O(V + E) time, which is O(rows x cols) on a grid.

Heaps. A heap is a complete binary tree stored in a Python list. In a min-heap the smallest item is always at the root, index 0. heapq.heappush and heapq.heappop take O(log n) because the item sifts up or down at most the height of the tree. Reading the smallest item, heap[0], is O(1).

Building a heap. heapq.heapify turns a list into a heap in O(n), not O(n log n). Most nodes sit near the bottom of the tree and sift down only a short distance; adding up the work over all levels gives at most about 2n swaps.

Dynamic programming (DP) is recursion plus memoization, or the same idea written bottom-up as a table. Use DP when the same subproblems appear again and again, as in fibonacci, coin change and longest common subsequence.

Campus wiki: Java JVM heap memory. The JVM heap stores Java objects. The -Xmx flag sets the maximum heap size, for example -Xmx2g. Garbage collection frees heap memory that is no longer used.
